oewn-00106028-r.learner: in a way that is done at the proper time, without delay.
examples: Mr. Collins readily assented, and a book was produced
The advice was followed readily, for the feverish symptoms increased, and her head ached acutely.
"You may readily comprehend," she added, "what my curiosity must be"
The path is readily found once you have crossed the bridge.

oewn-06799486-n.learner: words that tell someone how something is to be done.
examples: giving his housekeeper directions that every possible attention might be paid to the sick lady and her sister
tell my dear Lydia not to give any directions about her clothes till she has seen me

oewn-08697710-n.learner: a line that leads to a place or a point.
examples: They walked on without knowing in what direction.
She turned and walked off in the other direction.

oewn-13849639-n.learner: how a thing stands in space in relation to the course it points along or moves along.
examples: The direction of the wind changed during the night.
The needle shows the direction in which the ship is moving.

oewn-01452567-v.learner: to move something along while holding it up, either in your hands or on your body or in a vehicle.
examples: She would not listen, therefore, to her daughter's proposal of being carried home
"We have not quite determined how far it shall carry us," said Mrs. Gardiner

oewn-01063192-v.learner: to pass a message on to someone else.
examples: will you give yourself the trouble of carrying similar assurances to his creditors in Meryton

oewn-02642600-v.learner: to have or hold something you cannot touch, such as a thought or a feeling.
examples: by carrying with me one ceaseless source of regret in my sister's absence

oewn-00653662-v.learner: to be a feature, quality, or trait that sets someone or something apart; at times this is meant as high praise.
examples: there is that in her features which marks the young woman of distinguished birth
every sentence of her uncle, which marked his intelligence, his taste, or his good manners

connotation.why: picks a trait out as distinguishing rather than merely present

oewn-00509113-v.learner: to make a mark on something, or to leave one on it.
examples: The wet glass marked the polished table.

oewn-02122959-v.learner: to notice something, or to become aware of it.
examples: She marked the change in his manner as soon as he spoke.

oewn-06684229-n.learner: an idea you put to someone about the right thing to do.
examples: There is one point on which I want your advice.
Mr. Darcy took her advice, and did finish his letter.

oewn-00787849-n.learner: serious and careful work meant to do something or get something done.
examples: My courage always rises with every attempt to intimidate me.
with no further attempt to distinguish Elizabeth

oewn-00775311-n.learner: the act of attacking someone or something.
examples: The guards stopped an attempt on the king's life.

oewn-13876005-n.learner: the link between two things, based on the ways they are alike and the ways they differ.
examples: if Darcy were not such a great tall fellow, in comparison with myself, I should not pay him half so much deference
The death of your daughter would have been a blessing in comparison of this.

oewn-00143485-n.learner: the act of looking at things to see how they are alike.
examples: A careful comparison of the two letters showed that one hand had written both.

oewn-04754082-n.learner: the qualities in two things that make it possible to set one against the other.
examples: he is, beyond all comparison, the most agreeable man I ever saw
There is no comparison between the two singers.

oewn-03882197-n.learner: a work of art made by putting paint onto a surface.
examples: The picture had been painted in oils and hung above the fireplace.

oewn-07216464-n.learner: a description in words that is clear and full of life.
examples: It was Mr. Collins's picture of Hunsford and Rosings rationally softened
with Miss Austen the myriad, trivial, unforced strokes build up the picture like magic

oewn-03937282-n.learner: something made on a surface that shows an object, a scene, a person, or an idea.
examples: She drew a picture of the house on the back of the letter.
The old map had a picture of a whale in one corner.

oewn-00526673-s.learner: being only part of something, not the whole of it.
examples: observed Miss Bingley, in a half whisper
flying to her, cried in a half whisper, "I am glad you are come"

oewn-00519479-s.learner: being one of the two equal parts of something, in amount or in value.
examples: the two elder Miss Bennets were able to be for half an hour by themselves
it would be the death of half the good people in Meryton

oewn-00519960-a.learner: sharing only one parent, said of brothers and sisters.
examples: Her half sister has the same father but a different mother.
Follies and nonsense, whims and inconsistencies, do divert me, I own, and I laugh at them whenever I can.
to be so honestly blind to the follies and nonsense of others

connotation.why: names the behaviour foolish rather than merely odd

oewn-04898528-n.learner: the habit of acting in a stupid or hasty way.
examples: her ignorance and folly had contributed to his amusement

connotation.why: calls the trait stupid rather than merely bold

oewn-01250622-n.learner: a foolish mistake that someone makes.
examples: Selling the land so cheaply was a folly he regretted for years.

connotation.why: calls the mistake stupid rather than a plain error
